posts:
"Protecting the children" is the most effective skeleton key for unlocking private doors.

Keir Starmer Urges Tech Firms to Block Intimate Images
Evidence: child protection, mass scanning, state control
#Aletheia #Privacy #UK

The PM claims this is a targeted, moral necessity to prevent the exploitation of minors and ensure a safe digital environment.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

The mechanism required—breaking encryption or mass scanning—creates a permanent infrastructure for state surveillance of all citizens.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
The policy uses a high-pathos edge case to justify a systemic reduction in the privacy and security of the entire population.
UK PM Keir Starmer is threatening legislation if tech companies don't block children from sending or receiving intimate images within three months.

The Bright Side:
Reducing the circulation of self-generated child abuse material is a legitimate and urgent social priority that requires attention.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in the WHY (Q4). The stated "Why" is child safety, but the structural "How" necessitates the end of private communication.

It is a bait-and-switch: they promise "safety" but deliver "surveillance."

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Once the scanning infrastructure exists, its scope always expands beyond the original intent.

The Unavoidable Truth: You cannot have "secure" encryption that the government can also look inside.

The Unavoidable Lie: That this is only about the kids.

Alethekanon:
The proposal creates a structural vulnerability. By mandating a "backdoor" for morality, you create a front door for any future tyrant.

Awwthekanon:
We all want children to be safe from harm, but we must be careful not to build a world where no one has any privacy left at all.

Brothekanon:
The "think of the children" move is the oldest trick in the book. They want to read your DMs, and they're using a sad story to do it.
